items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I felt that when Marshall left Count Basie’s orchestra, the orchestra lost some of its character.

ctx.x: Yeah, but I mean, I think, at least listening to the recordings of your orchestra from . . . or any orchestra in which you played lead, there’s not that feeling of, you know, predominance of the lead alto. It’s sort of . . .
I wouldn’t call it predominance. I would call it authority, because that’s the way I always felt. I felt that when Marshall left Count Basie’s orchestra, the orchestra lost some of its character.
Maybe this is a good time, although you have answered this . . .
